text:
alex: Heads-up: HF->Redwood conversion for 'gptx-chat' failed on tool-calling tests. Tokenization mismatch is causing JSON-mode outputs to break. See attached logs.
mina: Can you paste the converted chat template + tokenizer special tokens? :thinking_face:
alex: Here are the relevant bits from the HF model config + what the converter produced. Short version: HF used explicit special tokens like '<|tool_call|>' and '<|json_mode|>', converter replaced them with angle-bracket tags and we lost the single-token property.
```json
// original hf_config.json (excerpt)
{
  "bos_token": "<s>",
  "eos_token": "</s>",
  "additional_special_tokens": ["<|tool_call|>", "<|json_mode|>", "<|role_assistant|>"]
}
```
```json
// converter output (redwood chat template / config)
{
  "system_prompt": "<tool name=search/> Use JSON_MODE_START ...",
  "special_tokens": ["<tool>", "<json>", "<role_assistant>"]
}
```
alex: The problem: tokenizer.vocab doesn't contain '<tool>' as a single token. During tokenization it's split into "<", "tool", ">" and the model emits pieces that break the JSON parser in downstream evals.
jasper: Right — the converter is collapsing HF's single-token markers into printable tags. HF special tokens are registered in tokenizer so encode/decode is idempotent. Our converter replaced the raw tokens instead of calling tokenizer.add_tokens(...) so we ended up with multi-token sequences.
sam: Quick fix idea: when converting, preserve the exact HF special token strings and call tokenizer.add_tokens(["<|tool_call|>"]) before saving the tokenizer. That way the special sequence remains atomic. Example: 
```py
# converter snippet
if hf_cfg.get('additional_special_tokens'):
    tokenizer.add_tokens(hf_cfg['additional_special_tokens'])
    tokenizer.save_pretrained(out_dir)
```
mina: There's also collision with role tokens and the JSON mode marker. Example: we had '<|json_mode|>' and '<|role_assistant|>' adjacent in templates which the tokenizer sometimes merges oddly after quantization, producing '<<|json_mode|>\nrole...' splits. Any ideas?
alex: We observed this mostly with 4-bit quantization builds (q4_k_m). With quantized weights + byte-pair merges changing slightly, some decode probabilities shift and the model emits a leading '<' as separate token more often, truncating JSON blobs. In our eval suite pass@1 on tool-calling went from 92% -> 78% for the converted+q4 model.
jasper: Repro step: run the tool-calling eval harness with the converted tokenizer and both w/ and w/o added special tokens. Command we used: 
```
./tools/eval_tool_calling.py --model converted_gptx --tokenizer out/tokenizer --quant q4 --prompt-set tool_calls_v2
```
jasper: pinging @ci-bot to run the job on the CI matrix (cpu/gpu, q4/q8).
ci-bot: CI queued: eval_tool_calling (converted_gptx, q4) — started.
ci-bot: CI finished: regressions found in tool-calling suite (json parse failures 24/100) — full report at https://ci.internal/runs/12345
alex: Temporary workaround: patch the runtime to post-process token streams and reassemble recognized angle-tag fragments into single pseudo-tokens before JSON parse. Ugly but blocks immediate crashes.
mina: Long-term fix proposals: 1) change converter to preserve HF special token strings and call tokenizer.add_tokens(...) 2) embed special_tokens list in the saved config so RW runtime knows to treat them atomically 3) add a converter flag --preserve-specials for backwards compat.
jasper: I'll draft a PR. Also adding a fuzz/unit test: ensure for each special token s -> tokenizer.decode(tokenizer.encode(s)) == s and ensure encode-decode idempotence across quantization configs.
alex: Also we should add a small benchmark to compare pre/post conversion BLEU/ROUGE on the tool-calling prompts and track pass@1. If CI shows big regression for q4, we should pin quantization until tokenizer fix lands.
sam: One more gotcha: some HF chat templates used control codes like '\\u0120' (whitespace markers) around tokens. Converter stripped them which changed merges. Keep an eye on whitespace normalization.
jasper: :thumbsup: PR will include: converter tests, tokenizer.add_tokens, preserved special_tokens in redwood config, and a regression check in our eval harness.
alex: Thanks everyone. Keep updates here. If CI regression is severe we'll revert q4 autoscale and rerun.
